scenes.script: A rainbow is not a thing in the sky. You can never reach it, and nobody else sees the one you see.
Most people think it is painted on the clouds, like a picture on a wall. But it is made fresh, inside falling rain, every moment.
Here is the real reason. Sunlight looks white, but it is a mix of every colour.
When sunlight enters a raindrop, it bends. Then it bounces off the back of the drop, and it leaves on the same side it came in.

items: It leaves on the same side

scenes.script: Each colour bends by a slightly different amount, so the white light fans out. Red leaves at one angle, and violet at another.
So each drop sends only one colour to your eye. Higher drops send red, lower drops send violet, and millions together draw the bow.
That is why the sun must be behind you. Try it with a garden hose: turn your back to the sun, and spray a fine mist.

cards.text: Sun behind you, rain in front

items: Turn your back to the sun

scenes.script: So the next rainbow you see is yours alone: light, sorted by water, and aimed at your own eyes.
